prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the 3D geometry of a narrow bathroom, showing the right wall (with its radiator) and left vanity edge as bright near surfaces (~0.3–0.8 m away), the tiled floor sloping away, and the back wall with a door and hanging towel as dark background regions (~2.0–2.5 m away). No other people are present, and after frame 1—where the camera points high and left while the dog is out of view below—a dog appears in the lower-right foreground about 0.2 m from the right wall and 1.0–1.5 m in front of the back door. Across frames 2 to 5, the dog's silhouette brightens as the camera wearer approaches and tilts down from ~1.2–1.5 m away to within arm's reach (~0.5–0.8 m), capturing the dog facing forward-left away from the camera in frames 2–3 before turning its head up toward the camera wearer in frames 4–5 while its hindquarters are cropped by the bottom-right frame edge. Compared to the RGB strip, the depth map clearly separates the dark-furred dog's 3D contour from the shadowed floor and wall corner, though it is unreliable along the bright distorted left lens border in frames 1–3 and smooths over small objects such as the metal bowl partially occluded beneath the dog in frames 4–5.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates only a single foreground mask per frame against an otherwise blank background, omitting the bathroom walls, floor, vanitywithin arm's reach on the left, and the small metal bowl next to the dog's front paw in frames 4–5. In frames 2–5, the mask tracks the dog in the lower-right foreground as the camera wearer moves from ~1.2–1.5 m away (frames 2–3) into arm's reach at ~0.5–0.8 m (frames 4–5), with the mask's growing footprint and bottom-right truncation showing the animal's lower body moving partly out of view. The mask contours reflect the dog facing away toward the back door in frames 2–3 and raising its head to look directly at the camera wearer in frames 4–5, while cleanly separating the dog's dark coat and front left leg from the adjacent floor shadows and metal bowl better than the dim RGB image alone. However, the map is semantically unreliable: it hallucinates a 'tie' on the motion-blurred wooden door (~1.5–2.0 m away) in frame 1, misclassifies the dog as a 'cat' in frames 2 and 4, and outputs overlapping 'cat' and 'dog' labels on the same animal in frames 3 and 5.
descriptions.pose: Because no visible people or hands are in the bathroom, the pose map is mostly empty and displays only erroneous yellow human-body keypoints in frames 1, 2, and 4 with no magenta hand skeletons in any frame. In frame 1, a cluster of disconnected yellow dots appears near the bottom-left vanity (~1.0–1.5 m away), while in frames 2 and 4 a compact yellow upper-body skeleton is placed over the dog in the lower-right foreground as the distance between the camera wearer and the animal decreases from ~1.2–1.5 m to within arm's reach (~0.5–0.8 m). In frames 2 and 4, the plotted shoulder-hip torso lines and clustered facial keypoints roughly align with the dog's back and head orientation—facing forward-left away from the camera in frame 2 and turned up toward the camera wearer in frame 4—while terminating above the dog's partially occluded and cropped hindquarters. This map provides no valid spatial detail beyond what is visible in the RGB image and is highly unreliable, hallucinating human joints on bathroom fixtures in frame 1, fitting a human torso-and-arm skeleton onto a quadruped in frames 2 and 4, and dropping out completely in frames 3 and 5.
